overview.title: Figures 4.6-4.7: Reuters loss and accuracy curves
overview.section: 4.2 Classifying newswires: A multiclass classification example
overview.main_topic: Training vs. validation loss and accuracy over 20 epochs for the 64-64-46 Reuters model
overview.central_idea: Training loss keeps falling and training accuracy keeps rising, but validation loss bottoms out around epoch 9 and validation accuracy plateaus near 82%: the model starts to overfit after about nine epochs.
overview.importance: These two plots are the evidence for the decision on p.147 to retrain from scratch for nine epochs.
learning_objectives: Read a pair of training/validation curves and locate the onset of overfitting
Relate the gap between training and validation accuracy to generalization
prerequisites: The IMDb curves and the definition of overfitting (p.137-138)

summary:
This page contains only two figures, the output of the training run in listing 4.18 (p.144).

**Figure 4.6, Training and validation loss** (produced by listing 4.19): the red dashed training loss starts near 3.3 at epoch 1 and decreases monotonically to about 0.1 by epoch 20. The solid blue validation loss starts lower (about 2.6), drops quickly to about 1.0 by epoch 5, reaches its minimum of roughly 0.88 around **epoch 9**, and then creeps back up to about 1.0 by epoch 20. The curves cross around epoch 3-4; after that the training loss is lower.

**Figure 4.7, Training and validation accuracy** (produced by listing 4.20 on p.146): training accuracy rises from about 0.40 to about 0.96 and flattens out. Validation accuracy rises from about 0.49 to a plateau of roughly **0.81-0.83** from epoch 8 onward, peaking slightly around epoch 12 before drifting down a little.

How to use the page: the widening gap between the curves after about epoch 9 is the signature of overfitting described for IMDb on p.138. The book states the conclusion on p.147: "The model begins to overfit after nine epochs", and retrains a fresh model for nine epochs. Note (not in the book): the validation loss turns upward earlier and more clearly than validation accuracy, which stays nearly flat; loss is sensitive to over-confident wrong predictions even when the argmax does not change.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.definition: Continued improvement on training data accompanied by stagnating or worsening performance on unseen data.
concepts.intuition: The model starts memorizing quirks of the 7,982 training newswires rather than learning patterns that transfer.
concepts.technical: Visible in figure 4.6 as validation loss rising after its minimum near epoch 9 while training loss keeps decreasing.
concepts.significance: Determines the training length used on p.147.
concepts.example: At epoch 20: training accuracy ≈ 0.96, validation accuracy ≈ 0.81.
concepts.misconception: Overfitting does not require validation accuracy to fall sharply; a flat validation accuracy with a growing train-validation gap and rising validation loss already indicates it.

deeper.title: Why validation loss rises while validation accuracy stays flat
deeper.body: Beyond the book: accuracy only checks whether the argmax is correct, while crossentropy measures $-\log$ of the probability on the true class. As training continues, the model grows more confident. On validation samples it gets wrong, that confidence makes $-\log \hat y_c$ very large, which pushes the mean validation loss up even if the number of correct argmaxes barely changes.

misconceptions.claim: Since training accuracy is 96%, the model will be about 96% accurate on new newswires.
misconceptions.correction: Validation accuracy (about 81-82%) is the relevant estimate; the test result on p.147 is about 80%.

takeaways: Training loss falls steadily from about 3.3 to about 0.1 over 20 epochs.
Validation loss is lowest near epoch 9 (about 0.88) and then rises.
Validation accuracy plateaus around 0.82 while training accuracy reaches about 0.96.
These curves justify retraining for nine epochs (p.147).

questions.question: In figure 4.6, at roughly which epoch does validation loss reach its minimum?
questions.explanation: The blue curve bottoms out at about 0.88 around epoch 9 and then rises. Epoch 3 is where the curves cross; at 15 and 20 validation loss is already increasing.

questions.question: Why does the training loss start above the validation loss at epoch 1 in figure 4.6?
questions.answer: The training loss for an epoch is averaged over batches while the weights are still being updated (starting from random weights), whereas validation loss is computed at the end of the epoch with the improved weights.
questions.explanation: This timing difference is not discussed on this page; it explains the early crossing of the curves around epoch 3-4. (AI explanation.)

questions.question: What is the approximate gap between training and validation accuracy at epoch 20 in figure 4.7?
questions.explanation: Read from the plateau levels of the two curves; the gap indicates the model fits the training data much better than it generalizes.

questions.question: Validation accuracy in figure 4.7 is nearly flat after epoch 9, yet the book says the model is overfitting. What evidence supports that?
questions.answer: Validation loss rises after epoch 9 in figure 4.6 while training loss keeps falling, and the train-validation accuracy gap keeps widening.
questions.explanation: Overfitting is defined by worsening generalization relative to training performance (p.138), and the loss curve shows it most clearly.

questions.question: Can you sketch, from memory, the shape of both curves in figure 4.6 and mark the epoch you would stop training at?
questions.answer: Training loss: steep decline flattening near 0.1. Validation loss: decline to a minimum around epoch 9, then slow rise. Stop around epoch 9.
questions.explanation: Compare your sketch with the figure; the stopping point matches the nine epochs used on p.147.
